title: 日本、アジア諸国の原油調達支援アピール　中国に依存しない経済安保強化　ASEAN＋3
extracted_text: 3日に開催された日中韓とASEANの財務相・中央銀行総裁会議で、片山さつき財務相はアジア諸国の原油調達への支援を強化する姿勢をアピールした。中東情勢の混乱を受け、中国は自国でのエネルギー確保を優先し、近隣国への燃料輸出を制限しているとされる。日本はこの間にアジア諸国との関係を強化し、中国に依存しない経済安全保障の枠組みに参加するよう促す。 「地域協力の必要性で一致した。助け合いながらサプライチェーン（供給網）多様化などに取り組む」。片山氏は会合後の記者会見でこう述べた。 高市早苗首相は4月、原油調達に苦しむアジア諸国の支援に約100億ドル（約1兆6千億円）を拠出すると表明した。米国など中東以外から原油を調達する際に金融面でサポート。さらに、バイオ燃料などエネルギー源の多様化や省エネの取り組みも促す計画だ。 日本は手術器具などの石油関連製品をアジアに頼っており、各国の支援を通じて供給網を維持したい狙いもある。日本政府高官は「そろそろ実際の案件にしていく時期」と話し、対象国が多く参加する今回の会議を機に支援の具体化を急ぐ。 これまで中国はインフラ投資や貿易の拡大でアジア諸国への関与を強めてきた。ただ今回の中東危機では自国のエネルギー確保を優先し、近隣国への石油製品の輸出を制限しているという。備蓄に手を付けず調達先の多角化で原油の大量輸入を続けているともされる。 中国を巡っては、レアアース（希土類）を含む重要鉱物の輸出管理などで経済的威圧を繰り返したり、過剰生産で安価な電気自動車（EV）や鉄鋼などを売りさばき世界市場をゆがめたりしているとの批判も根強い。 こうした中国の「身勝手なふるまい」（市場関係者）に、近隣国はほとほと不満を募らせる。日本はこのタイミングでアジア諸国に対する支援を打ち出すことで関係の深化を図る。各国に中国依存からの脱却を促し、日本との経済安保の枠組みに取り込みたい考えだ。（中村智隆）
translated_text: At the finance ministers and central bank governors meeting of Japan, China, Korea and ASEAN held on the 3rd, Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama expressed Japan's stance of strengthening support for Asian countries' crude oil procurement. Amid turmoil in the Middle East, China is said to be prioritizing its own energy security and restricting fuel exports to neighboring countries. Japan is using this period to strengthen its relations with Asian countries and encourage them to join an economic security framework not dependent on China. "We agreed on the need for regional cooperation and to work together on diversifying supply chains," Katayama said at a press conference after the meeting. Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi announced in April that Japan would contribute approximately $10 billion (about 1.6 trillion yen) to support Asian countries struggling with crude oil procurement. This would provide financial support when sourcing crude oil from regions outside the Middle East, such as the United States. The plan also calls for promoting diversified energy sources such as biofuels and energy conservation efforts. Japan relies on Asian countries for petroleum-related products such as surgical instruments, and aims to maintain supply networks through support from various countries. A senior Japanese government official said, "It's time to start turning this into actual projects," and expressed urgency to concretize support, using the current meeting with many participating countries as an opportunity. Until now, China has strengthened its involvement in Asian countries through infrastructure investment and trade expansion. However, during the current Middle East crisis, China is said to be prioritizing its own energy security and restricting exports of petroleum products to neighboring countries. It is also said to be continuing large-scale crude oil imports through diversification of supply sources without touching its reserves. Criticism also persists regarding China, including repeated economic coercion through export controls on important minerals including rare earth elements, and distorting global markets by selling cheaply priced electric vehicles (EVs) and steel through overproduction. Neighboring countries have grown quite exasperated with such "self-serving behavior" by China (according to market sources). Japan aims to deepen relationships by offering support to Asian countries at this timing. The idea is to encourage countries to break free from dependence on China and bring them into Japan's economic security framework. (Nakamura Tomotaka)
title_en: Japan Appeals to Support Asian Countries' Crude Oil Procurement, Strengthening Economic Security Not Dependent on China - ASEAN Plus 3
